title: Budget and Revenue
text:
this is a short introduction to the analysis of the relationship between movie budgets and revenues. Figure 1 shows the relationship between movie budgets and revenues.

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

df = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

plt.scatter(df["budget_musd"], df["revenue_musd"])
plt.xlabel("Budget (million USD)")
plt.ylabel("Revenue (million USD)")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Movie Budget vs Revenue

title: Runtime and Ratings
text:
this is a short introduction to the analysis of the relationship between movie runtimes and ratings.
Figure 1 shows the relationship between movie runtimes and ratings.

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

df = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

plt.scatter(df["runtime_min"], df["imdb_rating"])
plt.xlabel("Runtime (minutes)")
plt.ylabel("IMDB Rating")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Movie Runtime vs Ratings






df["decade"] = df["year"] // 10 * 10
df.groupby("decade")["imdb_rating"].mean().round(2)



Table 1: Mean IMDB Rating by Decade



decade
1980    8.01
1990    7.70
2000    7.94
2010    7.83
2020    7.44
Name: imdb_rating, dtype: float64

title: Revenue and Time
text:
this is a short introduction to the analysis of the relationship between movie revenue and time.
Figure 1 shows the relationship between revenue and time.

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

df = pd.read_csv("films.csv")


bond = df[df["franchise"] == "James Bond"]


plt.plot(bond["year"], bond["revenue_musd"])
plt.xlabel("Year")
plt.ylabel("Revenue (million USD)")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Revenue over Time





the first Bond year is 1995 and last Bond year is 2021.
